decisions.statement: A call is judged by the words the call is handed rather than by the call's name.
The words a list has are read as one command line.
A command written as one string is split on whitespace into that same word line.
A value put into a template is one word whose spelling is unknown.
The command run is the first word past the flags and the assignments `env` was given.
A word line whose command is unknown is left.
`BASH_ENV` given a value in the same call leaves that call alone.
`BASH_ENV` taken away in the same call leaves that call alone.
A file named `.sh` or `.bash` is read as a script a bash runs.
A call already refused is not read again through the arguments the call has.
A script whose first line names a shell reading no startup file is refused with the rest.
A shell file writing this call is judged by nothing here.

definition: the rule refusing an `env -u` scrub the bash startup file undoes before the command runs
